content: Highly Confidential to NAG and advisors – not fit for distribution
A brief, imprecise overview of the strategic background in which NAG is operating. This is not meant to provide
a strategic analysis but may facilitate in the development of one. This document can be read by NAG Strategic
advisors to get a sense of what the company is currently doing before real discussions can begin.
NAG has existed in some form since 1970 and has been a commercial company since 1976. The NAG Library, a
collection of numerical algorithms, has been the primary product and revenue generator through this period
and remains one of two major revenues streams today. Through the 1980s and 1990s NAG developed a strong
reputation in the area of numerical analysis and numerical software development. The product became world-
recognised, both in the user community and in the academic research community. Major academic / research
players contributed to the NAG Library in areas such as Statistics, Linear Algebra and Mathematical
Optimization. NAG remains strongly linked to world class researchers, such as Jack Dongarra (Manchester &
Tennessee  - HPC, Linear Algebra) Nick Higham (Manchester - numerical Analysis) and Uwe Naumann (RWTH
Aachen, Automatic Differentiation) to name just a few.
The NAG Library remained the strongest collection of algorithms through a competitive period, with IMSL
(Visual Numerics, now Perforce) the closest direct competitor, having a stronger presence in the US but weaker
in the UK and EMEA. Students were taught the NAG library in their Fortran and engineering undergraduate
courses and entered the workforce with knowledge of the product and its abilities. It remained well-recognised
and well regarded name in the field of numerical analysis and HPC and was used in a variety of Engineering

sections.heading: sectors.
content: Over the period 2000-2010 the NAG Library developed a strong customer base in sell-side Financial Services, as
the investment banks that developed their own pricing libraries required a robust and supported algorithmic
underpinning to their own codes. NAG today remains strongly embedded in a majority of the tier-1 banks and
several smaller banks. The financial sector is a rather impenetrable sector in which the customer’s technical
problems are not always articulated well for proprietary/competitive reasons. NAG has been unable to either
strongly tune the product to the needs of these customers, nor to capitalize on the market penetration by
developing successor products (with the except of the AD Suite, mentioned below). The financial clients are
mostly on perpetual licenses with limited annual service/support revenues for NAG.
During a similar period, the fundamental algorithms that affect processor performance (linear Algebra, FFTs,
RNGs) started being developed in-house by processor vendors to provide value-add to their products. These
companies could exploit more specific tunings for their own hardware and as such NAG could not develop

sections.heading: recruiting technical staff.
content: products that were competitive. This part of the NAG library’s business was lost, although NAG continues to
partner in the development of those libraries (e.g. Arm, Intel).
The Library business model has some natural limitations, it is a collection of user-agnostic functionality that
covers a broad mathematical spectrum. As such, traditional product management techniques that tailor the
product’s feature sets to a perceived need in the market, are difficult to apply. Content has sometimes been
added to the library according to the interests of the research community or opportunistic developments inside
the company, with little commercial awareness. Recent attempts to address this have been fraught with
obstacles. A trio of conditions make this problem difficult – the user-agnostic nature of numerical content, the
aggregation of content into the library format, and the proprietary nature of many of NAG’s clients.
NAG has over years attempted to develop or productise various other technologies, such as new compilers,
visualization frameworks and PDE solvers (twice). None of the new products has ever had any strong success.
However, the GenStat product that was spun-off to start a new company VSN has been mildly successful, and
NAG still owns a 25% stake in that company.
NAG has historically performed technical services alongside numerical library development, providing both an
alternative (minor) revenue stream and boosting library renewals. Major service work was established with
technology providers such as Intel, Arm and AMD, usually to develop some portion of their numerical software.
NAG developed the bulk of AMD’s ACML library in the early Opteron period. In the 2000s, NAG began providing
HPC services as an offering and established a major contract with HECToR, the UK national resource, to provide
CSE support. For approx. 7 years (2007-2014) NAG successfully established this service and the company
became both larger and financially very strong on the back of this. NAG was aggressively outbid in the HECToR
follow-on project called ARCHER, lost the business, and as a result went through significant reductions in staff.
Around 2010 NAG developed a relationship with an O&G major in Houston, through which a modest amount of
HPC service work ensued. Over a number of years NAG developed the relationship to the point of providing
continued HPC service provision on behalf of the client, a continual arrangement with >10 staff provided for
many years. This relationship has provided a sustainable revenue stream with strong margins for several years.
NAG has failed to replicate the model, which seems to be strongly tailored to the clients’ internal difficulties
NAG has provided a commercial Fortran compiler since the 1980s. It is world renowned in a niche setting –
strong support of the Fortran standard and error checking. It is used by many Fortran customers as a second,
supporting compiler to help development. It has never been a commercially lucrative product but provides
some reputational value to NAG.
NAG has commercialized the Automatic Differentiation products of RWTH Aachen. These products have found a
market within Financial Services. The company has reason to believe that automatic differentiation (similar to
back-propagation in Machine Learning) represents some real opportunity for NAG but this is yet to be realized.
The collaboration with RWTH Aachen is extremely strong and has been recently ramped up, NAG funds multiple
PhD positions there, with those students working part-time as engineers at NAG. The cost of sale of current the
product is high, revenues of the product remain low and penetration outside of FSI is low.
Brian Ford was NAG’s founder and CEO until 2005, Rob Meyer was CEO in the period 2005-2019 and Adrian
Tate is the current CEO. Since 2019, NAG has been undergoing a period of transformation, with changes to the
Executive team, collaboration style, development practices, emphasis on product, and marketing. The company
structure and culture have been drastically altered. Progress has been made in terms of innovation and
sustainability but many of NAG’s problems remain. In particular, the company is considered to have a lack of
focus, with too many balls in the air, too little time spent engaging with the market and too long spent talking

sections.heading: large technology providers.
content: In March 2022 NAG entered into a Framework Agreement with AMD that allowed AMD to make offers of
employment to NAG employees. For each employee that accepted the offer, NAG would be rewarded
financially. At the time of writing the transaction is yet to complete but is set to be quite successful. This style of
transaction is related to “acquihire” (where a company is acquired for its staff) which is a recent trend and a
reaction to the Great Resignation / global talent crunch. The scope of the deal means it is expected to drastically
accelerate the reprograming of NAGs internal dynamics and will increase profitability of the NAG Library. It is
expected that the replacements to departing staff will be at two levels a) junior staff to build the next
generation of engineers b) technical staff with more domain knowledge on how our products are used in the
market, to drive innovations.
The people that have moved to AMD have done so voluntarily, and with an enormous increase in benefits. The
transaction is much more amicable and positive than M&A activity.
Following the transaction, plus the existing healthy cash position, NAG has a cash balance of around 18 Million
GBP, which is expected to be used to invest in meet strategic aims. This should be a mixture of rebuilding to
support organic growth and inorganic activity to accelerate both growth and innovations. For those staff that
did not move, this growth and focus period will represent an exciting opportunity for the company.
We feel that our supplies of UK based technical talent remain open and that we could restaff any new
enterprise rather quickly. This leads to the potential for further Acquihire transactions with AMD or with other
NAG’s current strategic path has been around transformation. We have built missing capabilities and completely
reprogrammed the internal dynamics of the company. In an older company, change can happen too quickly so
this has been paced according to what the company can handle. We have built an innovation system, taken new
services to market, developed both Product Management and Product Marketing functions, started new
product discovery and new market discovery. Despite these successes, NAG is still too internal focused,
struggles with the market information needed to make product decisions, and is yet to display real success
outside the core areas of numerical software and managed services.
The NAG brand has been neglected over the years, and while there are some sectors that NAG has strong
reputation for its size, there are other sectors where the name is not well regarded. The company still looks old-
fashioned. Further improvements in presentation must be made, but the purpose of the company and the way
that it positions itself to the outside needs a reset. It will be important to not throw the baby out with the

sections.heading: bathwater.
content: NAG is primarily a products/technology company and will innovate to develop new IP in key areas. Candidate
areas are HPC technology in Cloud enablement, Optimization software targeting Portfolio Optimization, and
new AD products with a higher-level of abstraction. These product developments will be expensive, high-risk
and potentially dangerous for a company of this level. Ways to de-risk these efforts are central to NAG’s

sections.heading: sustainability plans.
content: One of NAG’s traditional strengths has been the cross-over of services and product development, meaning that
inefficiencies on both sides can be mitigated by staff moving between them. The recent success with acquihire
transactions means that NAG may have an interesting and unique path to further de-risking product offerings,
by including the option of such transactions in the paths to exit. New service offerings can be very difficult to
make sufficient margins due to consultant utilization, and new product offerings are naturally risky due to
product-market fit. NAG can explore acquihire transactions simultaneously to these other enterprises, which
means that when developments or new offerings do not become sufficiently profitable, then another route to

NAG’s status as a not-for-profit group is useful for these purposes, and for maintaining the collaborations with
